read_width caveats:
- No knob setting produced a resolvable per-access flash cost. At LATENCY = 0 a hit and a miss cost the same cycle, so every flash structure reads flat (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3) - over-program the wait states and re-run.

latch caveats:
- 2 configuration(s) are SILENT on this claim rather than evidence for or against it: waitstates=0 prefetch=0 loopmem=0, waitstates=0 prefetch=1 loopmem=1. In each the positive control fails - a hit and a miss differ by 0 cycles here (the same walk at `waitstates = 0`, where a flash access is known to cost no more than an SRAM one), below the 1-cycle resolution of an integer counter, so this configuration could not have shown a structure whether or not one is present - at LATENCY 0 in particular every flash structure reads flat by construction (MEASURING_CHANNELS B3) - so the flat column they produced is the resolution floor, not a register. A configuration that could not have shown the opposite does not get a vote.
- 2 configuration(s) show no data-side reuse at any offset - but in every one of them the probe loop is resident in the memory under test (waitstates=1 prefetch=0 loopmem=1, waitstates=1 prefetch=1 loopmem=1), so what vanished is the measurement, not the latch. They are excluded from 'does a register reach it', and they are the reason a run with the loop in flash reports the exact negation of the truth on a part with a unified cache.

cache caveats:
- No read width was resolved, so the eviction surface has no line to be fitted at.

replacement_policy caveats:
- LRU and FIFO are NOT separable with `memmap/1`'s two-argument primitives, and that is a property of the primitives rather than of the part. `walk` and `evict` produce a monotone reference string and `chase` a cyclic one, and on a cyclic string over capacity+1 lines LRU and FIFO evict exactly the same line at every step. Separating them needs a reference string that re-touches an already-resident line before bringing in a new one - which is what the optional third `evict` argument provides, and what a shim that does not implement it leaves unreachable.
- No multi-line cache was found, so there is no replacement policy to infer: a 1-entry latch has no victim to choose.

knob_map caveats:
- No read width or fill unit was resolved, so the data-reuse metric had no line to fit the eviction surface at and every data-reuse verdict is `unknown` rather than `no effect`.

waitstate_scaling caveats:
- No configuration was measured at three or more wait-state settings.

Cross-checks:
- Capture warnings: no advertised wait-state setting delivered a 4-cycle flash penalty (measured 0:0 1:0.032); the structural grid runs at the largest advertised setting (1) and hit/miss separation may be marginal
- SCOPE: every `evict` and `chase` row in this capture was taken at `waitstates = 1`, so the cache claim is a claim about that one setting. Nothing here suggests the geometry moves with the latency, and nothing here tests it either.
